issues.description: Method return-type mismatch for Pneumatic.raisePressure(int): the UML in problem_statement.md declares raisePressure(...): void (problem_statement.md line 17), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares boolean raisePressure(int) (solution/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java line 5) while the concrete classes LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster implement raisePressure with a void return type (solution/src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedDropdownTower.java line 10 and solution/src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedRollerCoaster.java line 10). This inconsistency (UML vs. solution interface, and interface vs. implementations) will cause compilation failures and confuses students which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the raisePressure(int) signature across all artifacts. Preferred fixes: (A) To follow the UML, change the solution interface to declare void raisePressure(int) and ensure LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster keep their void implementations; update the template Pneumatic.java to include 'void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease);'. OR (B) If a boolean return is intended, update the UML and the two implementing classes to return boolean (and adjust their method bodies to return a boolean), and update the template accordingly. Ensure tests and problem text reflect the chosen signature so students implement the correct method.
